title: Hydrodynamic Modeling of Flow Velocity and Sedimentation in the Tuyamuyun Channel Reservoir on the Amu Darya River
content: The article examines the hydrodynamic regime and siltation processes of the channel reservoir of the Tuyamuyun Hydro Complex, located in the lower reaches of the Amu Darya River. This facility operates under conditions of extremely high river flow turbidity, which leads to intensive sediment accumulation and a loss of the reservoir's capacity. Based on the equations of hydrodynamics and sediment transport theories, the spatio-temporal distribution of flow velocities has been calculated. The study accounted for factors such as seasonal fluctuations in water discharge, siltation of the backwater wedge zone, and changes in the morphometric characteristics of the reservoir under various operating modes. Critical zones of flow velocity decrease were identified, where the most active deposition of large and small fractions of suspended sediment occurs. The patterns of the reservoir channel's transformation during the filling and drawdown of its useful volume have been established. A quantitative assessment of the reservoir's siltation dynamics is provided. The results of the hydrodynamic calculation make it possible to forecast the rate of loss of the reservoir's regulating capacity and can be used to optimize sediment flushing regimes, prevent siltation of the near-dam area, and increase the operational reliability of the Tuyamuyun Hydro Complex structures.
